#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=nodes
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, conds:[.status.conditions[]|{t:.type,s:.status,r:.reason,m:.message}], allocCPU:.status.allocatable.cpu, allocMEM:.status.allocatable.memory, pods:.status.capacity.pods}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=deployments
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, rev:.metadata.annotations["deployment.kubernetes.io/revision"], env:[.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[]?|(.name+"="+(.value//""))], cpuLim:.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.cpu, memLim:.spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.memory}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash
# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables (unquoted slot),
# then reference them only as "$VAR" - never interpolate 
# inside a quoted context. See kubernetes_jq_query for the rationale.
KIND=pods
CUSTOM_COLUMNS=NAME:.metadata.name,NS:.metadata.namespace,NODE:.spec.nodeName,PHASE:.status.phase
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=null
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
FILTER_PATTERN=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""
[ "$FILTER_PATTERN" = "None" ] && FILTER_PATTERN=""

# kubectl ignores -n for cluster-scoped kinds; say so instead of reporting a namespace that wasn't applied
NOTES='[]'
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  is_kind() { awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind || index($1, kind ".") == 1 {found = 1} END {exit !found}'; }
  if kubectl api-resources --namespaced=false -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind \
    && ! kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind; then
    NOTES=$(jq -nc --arg note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${KIND} is cluster-scoped." '[$note]')
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
fi

SCOPE_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-n "$SEL_NAMESPACE")
else
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--all-namespaces)
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-l "$SEL_LABELS")
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

err_file=$(mktemp)
output=$(kubectl get "$KIND" "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" -o custom-columns="$CUSTOM_COLUMNS" 2>"$err_file")
kubectl_exit=$?
err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

SCOPE='null'
if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')
fi

if [ $kubectl_exit -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$output" ]; then
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    jq -n --arg stderr "$err_content" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
      '{count: 0, header: null, rows: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  else
    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Split header and data rows
header=$(echo "$output" | head -1)
if [ -n "$FILTER_PATTERN" ]; then
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2 | grep -E -- "$FILTER_PATTERN" || true)
else
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2)
fi

if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    count=$(echo "$data" | wc -l)
  else
    count=0
  fi
  # Rows go through stdin, not --argjson, so large tables don't hit "Argument list too long"
  printf '%s' "$data" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    --argjson count "$count" \
    --arg header "$header" \
    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
else
  echo "=== STDERR ==="
  echo "$err_content"
  echo "=== HEADER ==="
  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="
  echo "$data"
  echo "=== COUNT ==="
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then echo "$data" | wc -l; else echo 0; fi
fi

## 结论：两个已确认的故障 + 一个间歇性延迟问题

排查窗口：2026-11-16 15:12–15:16 UTC（日志：最近 30 分钟，各 Pod 当前容器日志；压测数据：loadgenerator locust 聚合输出）

---

### 根因 1（订单提交失败，100% 必然失败）：checkoutservice 的 cart 地址端口写错

- 线上 Deployment `checkoutservice` 实际值：`CART_SERVICE_ADDR=cartservice:7071`
- 但 `cartservice` Service 只暴露 **7070**（`port 7070 → targetPort 7070`），容器也只监听 7070
- 7071 上没有 Service 端口，kube-proxy 无规则 → 包被丢弃 → i/o timeout：

```
frontend: "failed to complete the order: rpc error: code = Internal desc = cart failure:
 failed to get user cart during checkout: ... dial tcp 10.96.234.227:7071: i/o timeout"
```
checkoutservice 自身启动日志直接印证：
```
service config: &{... cartSvcAddr:cartservice:7071 ...}   (15:13:36)
```
PlaceOrder 在第一步 `GetUserCart` 就失败，后面的支付/发货/邮件根本没被调用。

**这是镜像外的手工改动**：Deployment 的 `last-applied-configuration`（清单文件）里仍是正确的 `cartservice:7070`，live spec 是 7071；`checkoutservice-5d5f4589c5`(rev 53) 于 15:13:35 被 `checkoutservice-55cbbf7444`(rev 54) 替换 —— 即 15:13:35 有人对运行中的 Deployment 做了 `kubectl set env` 之类的漂移修改。

**修复**：
```bash
kubectl -n boutique set env deployment/checkoutservice CART_SERVICE_ADDR=cartservice:7070
# 或直接用仓库里的清单重新 apply，让 live 回到 last-applied 状态
```

---

### 根因 2（页面报错 / 体验降级）：adservice 被缩容到 0

- `Deployment/adservice`：`spec.replicas=0`，`Endpoints/adservice` 只有 `<none>`
- 事件：15:13:35 `ScalingReplicaSet Deployment/adservice Scaled down replica set adservice-6bfc5fc46c from 1 to 0` + `Killing/Stopped container server`
- 后果：前端每个页面（首页/商品页/购物车页）的广告调用都失败：

```
"failed to get ads: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... dial tcp 10.96.18.53:9555: connect: connection refused" (15:13:16 起持续，10 分钟内 ~220 条 warning)
```
页面还能渲染，但功能缺失且日志/连接开销持续存在。这是 scale-down（不是 HPA 引起的 template 变更；HPA 因 RBAC 禁止我无法列出，但 `spec.replicas` 本身被改成 0，符合手工 `kubectl scale`）。

**修复**：
```bash
kubectl -n boutique scale deployment/adservice --replicas=1
```

---

### 问题 3“时快时慢”：确认有间歇性延迟尖刺，根因指向 productcatalogservice 的间歇卡顿

locust 每接口统计（中位数 vs 最大值）——同一接口多数 10~13ms，但少部分请求冲到数百毫秒~1s：

| 接口 | 请求数 | 失败 | 中位 | 最大 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET `/` （首页） | 15 | 0 | 25ms | **84ms** |
| POST `/setCurrency` | 17 | 0 | 20ms | **96ms** |
| GET `/product/0PUK6V6EV0` | 11 | 0 | 13ms | **869ms** |
| GET `/product/2ZYFJ3GM2N` | 9 | 0 | 11ms | **856ms** |
| GET `/product/LS4PSXUNUM` | 35 | 0 | 11ms | **649ms** |
| GET `/cart` | 28 | 0 | 12ms | **657ms** |
| POST `/cart` | 26 | 0 | 15ms | **1080ms** |
| POST `/cart/checkout` | 11 | **8 (72.7%)** | 3ms | 53ms |

分析：首页和 setCurrency 从不尖刺；尖刺只出现在「商品详情页 / 购物车页 / 加入购物车」。这几个路径的共同新依赖是 **产品目录的 `GetProduct`**（首页用的是 `ListProducts`，setCurrency 不用目录）。关联证据：

- `Pod/productcatalogservice-7457c7c77f-rshp6` 事件 15:14:18 `Unhealthy: Readiness probe failed: timeout: failed to connect service "10.244.0.212:3550" within 1s`（连续 2 次）——该进程在探针 1s 时限内都没能应答 gRPC
- frontend 15:13:06 `could not retrieve products: ... dial tcp 10.96.32.253:3550: i/o timeout`（同一 Pod 的 ClusterIP 建连超时）
- 该 Pod 的 liveness/readiness 探针 `timeoutSeconds: 1`，而 CPU limit 只有 **200m**（request 100m），全集群 11 个 Pod 都跑在单节点 `tiktok-k8s-lab-control-plane` 上

**最可能的机制**：productcatalogservice（以及 frontend）被 CPU CFS 限流，出现周期性数百毫秒停顿 —— 这解释了「时快时慢」、0 失败率、以及探针 1s 超时的签名。
**未能证实**：我无法读取 CPU throttling / 节点指标 —— `kubernetes/live-metrics`、prometheus 工具集在本环境不可用，且 `nodes` 与跨命名空间 `pods` 列表对 `system:serviceaccount:diag-system:diag-agent` 是 Forbidden。确认方法：看 `container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total{namespace="boutique",pod=~"productcatalogservice.*|frontend.*"}` 以及节点 CPU 使用率。
**未完全排除**：cartservice/redis 路径（`/cart`、`POST /cart` 也经过它）—— 但 cartservice、redis-cart 日志无任何错误，cartservice 探针也没超时，所以证据弱于目录服务。

**建议修复**：把 `productcatalogservice`（及 `frontend`）CPU limit 从 200m 提高到 500m~1，request 提到 250m；单节点环境同时给 adservice Pod 留出 CPU。若尖刺消失即可确认限流假设。

---

### 影响范围分类

**受影响的（有本实体自身证据）**
- `checkoutservice`：`PlaceOrder` 全部失败（前端 ERROR 日志 + locust 72.7% 失败率）
- `frontend`：`POST /cart/checkout` 500、每页 `failed to get ads` warning（15:13:16 起持续）
- `adservice`：`Endpoints` 为空、Pod 被 `Killing`/`SuccessfulDelete`、`replicas=0` → 服务不可用
- `productcatalogservice`：自身 readiness 探针 `Unhealthy`（1s 超时 2 次）、以及一次被 frontend 记录的 3550 建连超时

**已检查、健康**
- `cartservice`、`redis-cart`、`currencyservice`、`paymentservice`、`emailservice`、`shippingservice`、`recommendationservice`：日志无错误（只有无害的启动 DeprecationWarning/pkg_resources 警告），Pod 全 Ready、restart 次数 0、无 OOMKilled
- 全部 11 个 Pod：`Ready=True`、`restartCount=0`，没有重启/OOM/驱逐

**窗口内变更但非本次故障**
- boutique 所有 Pod 于 15:12:45–15:12:46 重建（Deployment 创建时间是 11-15，ReplicaSet 未换版本、restart 0），符合节点/容器运行时重启后重建；事件已被 TTL 清理，无法进一步确认，不作为影响计
- `checkoutservice` 15:13:35 的 rev 53→54 滚动（由上述人工改 env 触发）

# Investigation guidelines

* Gather data with as many tool calls as needed before responding; keep going until you reach the deepest root cause you can find.
* Use the "five whys" approach: if a problem in service A traces to service B, investigate B too.

* Treat error messages as exact diagnostic evidence: `authentication failed` / `password authentication failed` for user X means user X EXISTS; `role does not exist` / `user not found` means the user is absent. These are mutually exclusive — never add "or the user may not exist" to an authentication failure.

# Impact and blast radius

* Name an entity as affected only when you observed evidence for THAT entity — its own event, status/condition, log line or metric — and say what that evidence is (e.g. "`checkout-cache`: Evicted event, now Pending").
* Never widen the blast radius by inference. A node condition does not tell you which pods it hit; a failing dependency does not tell you which of its clients broke; an unhealthy shared component does not mean its consumers are unhealthy. Check each entity before you name it, or do not name it — sampling a workload's replicas characterizes the WORKLOAD, so attribute what you found to it rather than to replicas you did not look at.
* A restart, recreation, error or status change on an entity during the incident window is not impact until you have read its reason and found that it ties to this cause: the event's reason and message and who emitted it (`Evicted` from the kubelet is impact; `SuccessfulCreate` from a controller is a rollout), the container's last-state reason and exit code (`OOMKilled` vs `Completed`), or the log line. A pod that is 5 minutes old on a node that had trouble 5 minutes ago was not necessarily evicted — check what created it. Coincidence in time is not causation, and "also affected" is a claim that needs its own evidence.
* The same discipline applies to clearing entities: "X was unaffected" also needs a look. If you did not check, say you did not check.
* Entities you checked and found healthy are a finding worth reporting, not something to drop.
* Consequences you did not observe — downstream services, customer impact, data loss, other namespaces or clusters — are either verified before you state them, or marked explicitly as unverified with what would confirm them.
* Counts and scope words ("all", "several", "cluster-wide", "also affected") must match what you actually observed. Do not generalize from a sample you did not take.
* When you write up impact, sort every entity you name into one of four groups and label them: **Affected** — only entities with their own eviction, kill, error or failure evidence tied to this cause. Every line here quotes the exact reason token that proves it, in parentheses: `Evicted`, `OOMKilled`, `BackOff`, `Failed`, `Unhealthy` on a long-running pod, an error log line. If you cannot quote such a token for that entity, it does not go here — `SuccessfulDelete`, `SuccessfulCreate`, `Scheduled`, `Started` and a probe miss at startup are not among them. A recreation, restart or probe miss inside the window is never enough on its own, whatever sub-label you give it; **Checked, healthy** — you looked and found nothing wrong; **Changed during the window for another reason** — it restarted, was recreated or errored, and you name what did it (a controller rollout, a scheduled job, an operator, a probe at startup) and how you know; **Not checked**. messages.reasoning_content:
Only checkoutservice env drift; adservice replicas=0 (was unset in applied, meaning manifest didn't specify replicas — but the deployment previously had 1, since RS-25 existed. Hmm, last-applied doesn't include replicas so `kubectl apply` wouldn't set it. adservice revision 25 and only one RS with desired 0 → the scale to 0 was a plain scale operation).

Interesting: adservice has only ONE replicaset with revision 25 — so no template churn, just replicas changed 1→0.

Now: were the pods at 15:12:45 recreated because of a node event? All pods restarted at 15:12:45 but RS's across deployments... cartservice rev 15 (created 11-15). Pods created 15:12:45 means pods were deleted and recreated then — probably a node reboot/kubelet restart (containerd restart) or someone deleted all pods. Events older than 1h are gone, but these events would be ~2 min old and still present... only 14 events exist, and none mention other pods being created at 15:12:45. Events have a default TTL of 1h but events for pods created 15:12:45 should still exist (Created/Scheduled/Started). They're not there! Hmm, only checkoutservice (15:13:35) pod's events are present.

Ah — events are probably in another ns? No. Maybe the events we see are only the latest 14 and others expired... The events list shows only 15:13:35+ ones. That means events from 15:12:45 were already gone, which would be odd within 3 minutes... unless there was an apiserver restart / event TTL short (some clusters set --event-ttl=5m? No, then checkout events remain but 15:12:45 is only 2 min old...).

Alternatively, the pod creations at 15:12:45 happened on a *different* node/API state, hmm. Or, this is a lab environment provisioned at 15:12 with a fresh cluster start (node boot), and events list is limited because the etcd data was reset... Honestly, the lab is a "tiktok-k8s-lab" sandbox — pods likely recreated when the whole environment was reset/provisioned (e.g., k3d cluster restarted, deployments re-applied? but deployment creationTimestamps are 11-15).

The pods' creation at 15:12:45 across ALL deployments simultaneously, with RS revision numbering already high — suggests a container runtime/kubelet restart or node reboot: pods get recreated after node restart. This explains "everything restarted at once" without deployment changes.

That's context (not necessarily impact). But wait: is that the cause of "时快时慢"? A node reboot 3 minutes ago, with cold caches... nah.

Now let me decide the final story. Also mention: adservice was terminated at 15:13:35 ("Killing" + "SuccessfulDelete" from RS controller), 3 minutes after the pods came up.

Regarding slowness, I should present the strongest evidence-based hypothesis. Let me reconsider once more: could the ad-service outage cause *page latency* in the demo? For the home page and product page, yes it produces a warning but the page renders. But! In frontend v0.10.3, `homeHandler` calls `fe.getAds` — and the gRPC call to a ClusterIP with NO endpoints: kube-proxy iptables REJECT → immediate refusal. And indeed logs show refusal instantly.

So ads ≠ slowness.

What about checkout POST also being counted as slow? Not slow (11ms avg).

So the slow things: /product pages (max 216–869ms), /cart GET (657), POST /cart (1080), /product pages 235-433.

Common: productcatalogservice.GetProduct. Plus cartservice for /cart and POST /cart.

I could check whether cartservice is slow by looking at redis-cart... but the cart page needs GetProduct per item anyway.

I'll present: two confirmed faults + one intermittently manifested latency issue whose most likely cause is productcatalogservice stalls (evidenced by 2 readiness-probe 1s-deadline timeouts at 15:14:18 and one 3550 dial timeout at 15:13:06), with node-level CPU contention as an alternative/unverified contributor. Recommend: check `container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total` for productcatalogservice/frontend, raise CPU limits, and note live-metrics toolset is disabled so I couldn't measure.

Hmm, but honesty: is 2 probe timeouts enough? It's the best signal available. Also note frontend CPU limit 200m.

Wait — one more possibility worth checking quickly: does the pod restart at 15:12:45 mean the node was rebooted and thus page caches cold? Not a root cause for intermittent slowness.

Actually, hold on. Let me reconsider the "时快时慢" from a user perspective: users browsing product detail pages see pages that sometimes take ~0.5–1s. Also the checkout page: /cart/checkout fails. Users may perceive "checkout page slow" because failures.

Let me quantify the slow-request rate: roughly 1-2 outliers per endpoint with ~10-30 requests → ~5-10% of requests >200ms. Median 11ms.

One more check that could be decisive: does the loadgenerator log per-request latencies? No, only aggregates.

Alternatively — check the frontend logs' timestamp density around a slow event? Not measurable.

I'll finalize. Also I should report entities checked/healthy: cartservice, redis-cart, currencyservice, paymentservice, emailservice, shippingservice, recommendationservice — no errors in their logs (I checked cartservice, redis, recommendationservice, productcatalogservice; not paymentservice/emailservice/shippingservice/currencyservice logs). Since checkout never reaches payment/email/shipping (it fails at GetUserCart first), those are untested. I should say I did not check them (payment/email/shipping/currency logs) — or quickly check them? They're small. Let me check paymentservice, shippingservice, emailservice, currencyservice logs quickly to be able to say they're clean.

Let me do that in parallel (4 calls), then write up.

Also worth noting pod restarts: the whole boutique namespace pods were recreated at 15:12:45–15:12:46 (startup time), 0 restarts — likely node/runtime restart; I can mention as context, labeled as "changed during window for another reason / not confirmed as impact."

## 结论：两个已确认的故障 + 一个间歇性延迟问题

排查窗口：2026-11-16 15:12–15:16 UTC（日志：最近 30 分钟，各 Pod 当前容器日志；压测数据：loadgenerator locust 聚合输出）

---

### 根因 1（订单提交失败，100% 必然失败）：checkoutservice 的 cart 地址端口写错

- 线上 Deployment `checkoutservice` 实际值：`CART_SERVICE_ADDR=cartservice:7071`
- 但 `cartservice` Service 只暴露 **7070**（`port 7070 → targetPort 7070`），容器也只监听 7070
- 7071 上没有 Service 端口，kube-proxy 无规则 → 包被丢弃 → i/o timeout：

```
frontend: "failed to complete the order: rpc error: code = Internal desc = cart failure:
 failed to get user cart during checkout: ... dial tcp 10.96.234.227:7071: i/o timeout"
```
checkoutservice 自身启动日志直接印证：
```
service config: &{... cartSvcAddr:cartservice:7071 ...}   (15:13:36)
```
PlaceOrder 在第一步 `GetUserCart` 就失败，后面的支付/发货/邮件根本没被调用。

**这是镜像外的手工改动**：Deployment 的 `last-applied-configuration`（清单文件）里仍是正确的 `cartservice:7070`，live spec 是 7071；`checkoutservice-5d5f4589c5`(rev 53) 于 15:13:35 被 `checkoutservice-55cbbf7444`(rev 54) 替换 —— 即 15:13:35 有人对运行中的 Deployment 做了 `kubectl set env` 之类的漂移修改。

**修复**：
```bash
kubectl -n boutique set env deployment/checkoutservice CART_SERVICE_ADDR=cartservice:7070
# 或直接用仓库里的清单重新 apply，让 live 回到 last-applied 状态
```

---

### 根因 2（页面报错 / 体验降级）：adservice 被缩容到 0

- `Deployment/adservice`：`spec.replicas=0`，`Endpoints/adservice` 只有 `<none>`
- 事件：15:13:35 `ScalingReplicaSet Deployment/adservice Scaled down replica set adservice-6bfc5fc46c from 1 to 0` + `Killing/Stopped container server`
- 后果：前端每个页面（首页/商品页/购物车页）的广告调用都失败：

```
"failed to get ads: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... dial tcp 10.96.18.53:9555: connect: connection refused" (15:13:16 起持续，10 分钟内 ~220 条 warning)
```
页面还能渲染，但功能缺失且日志/连接开销持续存在。这是 scale-down（不是 HPA 引起的 template 变更；HPA 因 RBAC 禁止我无法列出，但 `spec.replicas` 本身被改成 0，符合手工 `kubectl scale`）。

**修复**：
```bash
kubectl -n boutique scale deployment/adservice --replicas=1
```

---

### 问题 3“时快时慢”：确认有间歇性延迟尖刺，根因指向 productcatalogservice 的间歇卡顿

locust 每接口统计（中位数 vs 最大值）——同一接口多数 10~13ms，但少部分请求冲到数百毫秒~1s：

| 接口 | 请求数 | 失败 | 中位 | 最大 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET `/` （首页） | 15 | 0 | 25ms | **84ms** |
| POST `/setCurrency` | 17 | 0 | 20ms | **96ms** |
| GET `/product/0PUK6V6EV0` | 11 | 0 | 13ms | **869ms** |
| GET `/product/2ZYFJ3GM2N` | 9 | 0 | 11ms | **856ms** |
| GET `/product/LS4PSXUNUM` | 35 | 0 | 11ms | **649ms** |
| GET `/cart` | 28 | 0 | 12ms | **657ms** |
| POST `/cart` | 26 | 0 | 15ms | **1080ms** |
| POST `/cart/checkout` | 11 | **8 (72.7%)** | 3ms | 53ms |

分析：首页和 setCurrency 从不尖刺；尖刺只出现在「商品详情页 / 购物车页 / 加入购物车」。这几个路径的共同新依赖是 **产品目录的 `GetProduct`**（首页用的是 `ListProducts`，setCurrency 不用目录）。关联证据：

- `Pod/productcatalogservice-7457c7c77f-rshp6` 事件 15:14:18 `Unhealthy: Readiness probe failed: timeout: failed to connect service "10.244.0.212:3550" within 1s`（连续 2 次）——该进程在探针 1s 时限内都没能应答 gRPC
- frontend 15:13:06 `could not retrieve products: ... dial tcp 10.96.32.253:3550: i/o timeout`（同一 Pod 的 ClusterIP 建连超时）
- 该 Pod 的 liveness/readiness 探针 `timeoutSeconds: 1`，而 CPU limit 只有 **200m**（request 100m），全集群 11 个 Pod 都跑在单节点 `tiktok-k8s-lab-control-plane` 上

**最可能的机制**：productcatalogservice（以及 frontend）被 CPU CFS 限流，出现周期性数百毫秒停顿 —— 这解释了「时快时慢」、0 失败率、以及探针 1s 超时的签名。
**未能证实**：我无法读取 CPU throttling / 节点指标 —— `kubernetes/live-metrics`、prometheus 工具集在本环境不可用，且 `nodes` 与跨命名空间 `pods` 列表对 `system:serviceaccount:diag-system:diag-agent` 是 Forbidden。确认方法：看 `container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total{namespace="boutique",pod=~"productcatalogservice.*|frontend.*"}` 以及节点 CPU 使用率。
**未完全排除**：cartservice/redis 路径（`/cart`、`POST /cart` 也经过它）—— 但 cartservice、redis-cart 日志无任何错误，cartservice 探针也没超时，所以证据弱于目录服务。

**建议修复**：把 `productcatalogservice`（及 `frontend`）CPU limit 从 200m 提高到 500m~1，request 提到 250m；单节点环境同时给 adservice Pod 留出 CPU。若尖刺消失即可确认限流假设。

---

### 影响范围分类

**受影响的（有本实体自身证据）**
- `checkoutservice`：`PlaceOrder` 全部失败（前端 ERROR 日志 + locust 72.7% 失败率）
- `frontend`：`POST /cart/checkout` 500、每页 `failed to get ads` warning（15:13:16 起持续）
- `adservice`：`Endpoints` 为空、Pod 被 `Killing`/`SuccessfulDelete`、`replicas=0` → 服务不可用
- `productcatalogservice`：自身 readiness 探针 `Unhealthy`（1s 超时 2 次）、以及一次被 frontend 记录的 3550 建连超时

**已检查、健康**
- `cartservice`、`redis-cart`、`currencyservice`、`paymentservice`、`emailservice`、`shippingservice`、`recommendationservice`：日志无错误（只有无害的启动 DeprecationWarning/pkg_resources 警告），Pod 全 Ready、restart 次数 0、无 OOMKilled
- 全部 11 个 Pod：`Ready=True`、`restartCount=0`，没有重启/OOM/驱逐

**窗口内变更但非本次故障**
- boutique 所有 Pod 于 15:12:45–15:12:46 重建（Deployment 创建时间是 11-15，ReplicaSet 未换版本、restart 0），符合节点/容器运行时重启后重建；事件已被 TTL 清理，无法进一步确认，不作为影响计
- `checkoutservice` 15:13:35 的 rev 53→54 滚动（由上述人工改 env 触发）
messages.reasoning_content:
Those are benign startup deprecation warnings. payment/email/shipping/currency: no real errors.

Now let me think about whether to dig more on latency. One more idea: check productcatalogservice's History of readiness probe failures count — only 2. And check if the frontend had "could not retrieve products" only once.

Better idea! Check the checkoutservice — it also calls productcatalogservice.GetProduct during PlaceOrder, but PlaceOrder fails before that (GetUserCart first). Not useful.

Another idea: recommendationservice calls productcatalogservice.ListProducts; it logs errors if fails. No errors.

I think I should also consider: is the ~1s spike pattern actually caused by the frontend's *cart page* rendering many product images? No, loadgenerator requests are HTML only.

Let me try one more decisive check: compare `GET /product/66VCHSJNUP` (max 15ms!! avg 11ms over 8-9 requests) vs others which spiked. So some product endpoints never spiked (small sample). /product/66VCHSJNUP had 8-9 reqs, max 15ms — remarkably uniform. So spikes are sporadic across pages, i.e., not endpoint-specific but time-specific — a transient global stall affecting whichever requests were in flight. Home page (15 reqs spread over the run) never hit a stall — hmm, that's odd if stalls are global. But home requests are quick to be served... a stall would still delay them.

Wait: what if the stall is in productcatalogservice only, and the home `ListProducts` result is cached? No.

Hmm, actually, what if the stall is in cartservice? Product page also calls getCart (for cart badge), home too.

Alternatively the stall is in the *recommendation* service: product page + cart page call it; home doesn't; POST /cart doesn't... POST /cart 1080ms kills that.

So the intersection set: home calls {currency, catalog List, cart, ads}; setCurrency calls {currency convert}; product page calls {catalog GetProduct, currency, cart, recommendations, ads}; cart page calls {cart, catalog GetProduct(per item), shipping quote, currency, recommendations}; POST /cart calls {catalog GetProduct, cart insert}.

Slow: product page, cart page, POST /cart. Fast: home, setCurrency.
- Not common to slow ones: recommendations (not in POST /cart), shipping (only cart), ads (also home), currency (also home), cart (also home!), catalog GetProduct (only in slow ones) ✓✓✓.

Unless home doesn't call cart (then cart also qualifies: cart in product page, cart page, POST /cart insert — yes! cart is in all three slow ones and NOT in home if home doesn't call getCart, and not in setCurrency). Hmm. So candidates: catalog GetProduct OR cartservice/redis.

Distinguishing: productcatalog readiness-probe timeouts (2, at 1s deadline) → evidence of catalog stall. Is there similar evidence for cartservice? No probe failures for cartservice; its probes (grpc 7070) never timed out. And cartservice logs show no delays/errors, redis-cart logs clean.

But careful: cartservice's readiness probe... the events list didn't show cartservice Unhealthy. So catalog is the better-supported candidate. Good: productcatalogservice does GetProduct, and it's the one pod with measured stalls (probe timeouts at 15:14:18, plus the frontend's dial timeout to 10.96.32.253:3550 at 15:13:06 — the same pod's ClusterIP).

So my write-up: leading cause of "时快时慢" = productcatalogservice intermittently stalling. Note the ambiguity (cartservice not ruled out), and that CPU throttling under 200m limit is plausible but unverified (metrics unavailable).

Hmm, one more thought — could the catalog stall be caused by CPU limit 200m plus it being called by both frontend and recommendationservice? Yes, that's consistent: it's the busiest pod, tightest limit.
